text:
Jordan (CS): FYI noticed a small but persistent latency drift for BrightBridge during the onboarding traffic spike yesterday. Might impact their 99th pct SLO if it continues. @Priya can we flag this for renewal risk review?
Priya (Success): Thanks — saw the alert this morning. Is it steady or a few noisy tails?
Sam (SRE): saw the tails. 99p moved from 420ms -> ~1.1s for a 30m window around 03:15 UTC. baseline 95p/median unchanged. looks like batching contention on their Dedicated pool.
latency-monitor-bot: alert: slo_violation_risk BrightBridge model-pool-dedicated-7 window=30m 99p=1100ms threshold=1000ms
Jordan (CS): ok that's borderline. BrightBridge's contract has a 99th pct latency SLO at 1s with 3mo lookback for credits. If this repeats we should prepare comms.
Maya (Onboard Eng): I can run a quick profile with their sample workload and adjust batching config. need a window when they run their next ingestion job.
Priya (Success): Can we get a short customer note ready? Recommend: acknowledge, share current metrics, say we're investigating, and timeline for follow-up. keep it high-trust.
Sam (SRE): Action plan: 1) profile request pattern, 2) test bump to smaller batch cap, 3) if regression fixed, roll to prod on pool; otherwise switch to fallback pool to meet 99p. ETA for initial test: 6 hours.
Jordan (CS): I'll draft the note. Quick question: do we owe them any immediate credits under the SLA rules? Last quarter they had one small downtime credit but no latency credits.
Priya (Success): SLA credit calc: credits apply if monthly SLO breaches exceed threshold. single short tail w/o rolling monthly breach = no auto-credit, but customers expect transparency. we should offer a proactive credit if pattern repeats before renewal.
Jordan (CS): Draft to customer v1: "Hey BrightBridge — we observed elevated tail latency during a short window yesterday affecting a subset of requests. Our SREs are investigating, we've identified batching contention as likely cause, and we'll share mitigation and timeline within 8 hours. We take SLA commitments seriously and will follow up with remediation and any applicable credit calculations." Thoughts?
Maya (Onboard Eng): looks fine. add a line offering a 1:1 runbook walkthrough for their engineering team so they can avoid heavy burst patterns during onboarding.
Sam (SRE): also add: we can temporarily route their prod-origin traffic to a lower-latency fallback while we tune. need ops approval for reroute — tagging @oncall.
Jordan (CS): good — I'll include that. Priya, want to own the customer send and renewal note?
Priya (Success): I'll send initial note after Sam posts test results. if the test confirms fix we'll include remediation steps and no credit. if issue persists we'll calculate the prorated latency credit and present options.
latency-monitor-bot: note: next alert window scheduled 6h from now for pool-dedicated-7
Jordan (CS): thanks team. Action items: Sam run profile + test (ETA 6h), Maya prep runbook offer, Priya draft & send comms after test. I'll add renewal-risk flag to the account dashboard and capture as an enablement action for the CSM checklist.
Sam (SRE): starting profiling now, will push logs and a short gif of the profiler to the thread.
Priya (Success): tagging renewal: @sales_lead to FYI — may need to surface during renewal call.
Jordan (CS): perfect. Let's keep notes concise in this thread so we have an audit trail for SLO evidence. :thumbsup:
